newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL SENATE TO VOTE ON NEW CENTRAL BANK CHIEF.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL SENATE TO VOTE ON NEW CENTRAL BANK CHIEF.

text.p: The Brazilian Senate will vote Tuesday afternoon on the nomination of Gustavo Franco as the next president of the Central Bank, officials said.

A Senate official said the voting session was likely to begin at 1530 local/1430 EDT/1830 GMT. Franco's nomination is last on the agenda but the government intends to reverse the order of items and hold the ballot on Franco first, he said.
Franco, a 41-year-old economist who is currently the Central Bank's Director of International Affairs, was approved by the Senate Economic Affairs Committee last week.

In a four hour panel hearing, Franco defended current economic policies and apparently won over senators who have previously criticized the bank's tight monetary policies and its foreign exchange policies that are based on a strong reais currency.
Tuesday's Senate vote will be by secret ballot and local news wires predicted Franco's name would pass easily.
Newspapers said Franco would assume the presidency of the Central Bank from the outgoing Gustavo Loyola in a formal ceremony next week.
